liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Garcia sounds joyous and rowdy; reviewer points to his fills after the last two sung lines of the final chorus [5]
- **Easy To Love You** (1 review): Described as the token Brent song of the night [9]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): The roughly 35-minute Scarlet–Fire–Playin' stretch is called top-notch, with the Rhythm Devils on form [16]
- **Playing In The Band** (1 review): Reviewer loves the well-played pre-drums segment, though some find the tempo a bit fast [16]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-05-30.sbd.miller.92217.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 19 songs; 141 min; rated 2.33/5 by 6 [1]. Said about its sound: Soundboard has weak low end; Lesh is essentially inaudible; Soundboard lacks Phil's bass, and Garcia only comes up in the mix about three-quarters through Jack Straw; Phil cannot be heard on the soundboard, though the band sounds locked in as if he were present [8][9][14]
- **gd80-05-30.aud.vernon.14837.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 136 min; rated 2.25/5 by 4 [2]. Said about its sound: Audience recording has serious azimuth problems and muffled audio that make it hard to listen to [6]
- **gd1980-05-30.128381.naks.mason.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 141 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds this a big improvement over the older copy on the site and an early-nineties cassette [10]
- **gd1980-05-30.set2.sbd.miller.91932.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 10 songs; 76 min [4]

## Around the show

- Hearing the opening of Jack Straw, the reviewer left the back of the floor for the first 15 rows [5]
- The band was rained out at Milwaukee's Summerfest on 7-2-78; the festival had to pay their guarantee and resented it [7]
- Reviewer says police set up a small station with a holding cell in the basement and arrested concertgoers in rows [7]
- Reviewer jokes that Alabama Getaway kept turning up as the closer throughout 1980 [12]
- Reviewer recommends the Pine Knob show from Summer Tour 1980 as an unexpected treat [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-05-30.sbd.miller.92217.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Set 1: Charlie Miller, Set 2: Rob Eaton, All Mastering by Charlie Miller; source: Set 1: SBD -> ? -> 5th Gen Cassette DSet 2: SBD -> Master Cassette -> Reel -> Dat (48k) [1]. Also: Set 1 comes from a cassette from Matt Smith, with Joe B. Jones helping on pitch correction; Gaps in Passenger, Easy To Love You, Not Fade Away and Alabama Getaway are filled from a cassette-to-DAT-to-CD source, shnid 14837 [1]
- **gd80-05-30.aud.vernon.14837.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [2]. Also: Audience source labeled A:C:C:D, passed via CDR from David Minches, with shn encoding by Matt Vernon [2]
- **gd1980-05-30.128381.naks.mason.flac16**: taped by Mason B. Taylor; source: Recorded By Mason Taylor on a Nakamichi 550 Cassette Deck, on chrome tapes, with Nakamichi microphones [3]. Also: Mason-sourced tape shared by his friends and family, in honor of Mason [10]
- **gd1980-05-30.set2.sbd.miller.91932.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller - Thanks to Rob Eaton for transferring his Dat; source: SBD -> Master Cassette -> Reel -> Dat (48k) D [4]. Also: Short sections of Not Fade Away and Alabama Getaway are patched in from the shnid 14837 source [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by May: [Vintage The Grateful Dead "Milwaukee Auditorium" Friday, May 30th 1980 Cardboard Back Poster](https://jointcustodydc.com/products/vintage-the-grateful-dead-milwaukee-auditorium-poster) [18]
- Fan art by May: [Vintage The Grateful Dead "Milwaukee Auditorium" Friday, May 30th 1980 Cardboard Back Poster](https://jointcustodydc.com/products/vintage-the-grateful-dead-milwaukee-auditorium-poster) [19]
- Poster by May: [Vintage The Grateful Dead "Milwaukee Auditorium" Friday, May 30th 1980 Cardboard Back Poster](https://jointcustodydc.com/products/vintage-the-grateful-dead-milwaukee-auditorium-poster) [20]
